<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `137018f279a2ed970ec84587d0dc1f4e0941e66d` — the merge of head `e88a8ecb3bd075e3a0a619006960ae90b74ede21` into base `2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 137018f279a2ed970ec84587d0dc1f4e0941e66d && git checkout 137018f279a2ed970ec84587d0dc1f4e0941e66d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5 e88a8ecb3bd075e3a0a619006960ae90b74ede21 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5 && git merge --no-ff e88a8ecb3bd075e3a0a619006960ae90b74ede21

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e88a8ecb3bd075e3a0a619006960ae90b74ede21`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts (`runIsOutsideFlow`, the five `/:name/runs/:runId/*` doors, `classifyResumeResult`, `RESUME_REFUSAL_ROWS`, `RESTORE_REFUSAL_STATUS`), packages/spec/scripts/check-error-code-provenance.ts (`STAMP_PATTERNS`, the gate the new row satisfies), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (the `error` builder and its `details.code` promotion), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (lines 6764 and 8572, the two engine sentences the door copies), packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-run-flow-scope.test.ts, the two adjusted pins (automation-resume-caller-gate.test.ts, automation-screen-read-gate.test.ts), .changeset/25820-automation-run-doors-flow-scope.md

Inputs: card #25820 body and all four comments (triage 6399818476, claim 6407766839, surface amendment 6407846633, os-dev-report 6408572060), PR #25944 body and file list, `git diff origin/main...origin/pr-25944` at the head (6 files, +350/-9), and the check-runs on the head. Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **A second producer row for an already-registered code is not a public-surface change — right.** `RUN_NOT_FOUND` was registered under `@objectstack/service-automation` (ledger line 1254) before this PR; the new row under `@objectstack/runtime` adds a package to the provenance half only. `ErrorCode` and `REGISTERED_ERROR_CODES` are the deduped union, so the accept set `ApiErrorSchema.code` parses against is byte-identical; the generated `content/docs/references/api/error-code-ledger.mdx` lists that union (no per-package section), so no regenerate is owed and none is missing. The one type-level difference, the `as const` tuple for `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER['@objectstack/runtime']` gaining a member, is a shape no schema or consumer parses against. The ledger header's own rule ("a code emitted by several packages is listed once per emitting package — provenance, not identity") is what this row does. `Clause-②: no` stands, as amendment 6407846633 measured.

2. **The row is owed, not decorative — right.** `check:error-code-provenance` reads three stamp shapes (`objlit`, `assign`, `constdef`). On `main`, `@objectstack/runtime` stamps the string nowhere the gate sees: the `RESUME_REFUSAL_ROWS` map key and the `RESTORE_REFUSAL_STATUS` object key are not stamp shapes and `details.refusal` is not `code:`. At the head, `const RUN_NOT_FOUND_CODE = 'RUN_NOT_FOUND'` is a `constdef` site attributed to runtime, so without the row the gate reds. No `PROVENANCE_WAIVERS` pair exists for (runtime, RUN_NOT_FOUND), so the row is not dead weight against a waiver. The row comment names the resume and run-read doors only, which is accurate: the restore door relays the engine code in `details.refusal` deliberately, never `details.code`, and the screen and cancel doors stamp no code.

3. **The 404 bodies for "exists but not owner" and "unknown flow" are identical, and identical to the unknown-run answer — right.** Resume: both reach `runIsOutsideFlow` as `true` (an unknown flow owns nothing; no earlier flow-existence check sits in the `:name/runs/:runId` arms, which the suite proves with `no_such_flow`), then `classifyResumeResult(unknownSuspendedRun(runId))` matches the `RUN_NOT_FOUND` row and returns before `resumeFailureDetails`, so no `inspectConsumedSuspension` probe runs and nothing in the body depends on whether the run exists. Message `No suspended run 'RUNID'`, status 404, `details.code` promoted to `error.code` by the dispatcher builder. The real engine spells its unknown-run refusal the same way at `engine.ts:6764`. Run-read: both arms answer `deps.error('Execution not found', 404, { code: 'RUN_NOT_FOUND' })`. The suite pins mismatch equals unknown-flow, and mismatch equals nobody's-run with the id masked, on all five doors.

4. **The run-read door's unknown-run code moves from the status-derived `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` to `RUN_NOT_FOUND` — a wire change on one door, right under the ruling, and not a face change.** Both values are already members of the published face, so the accept set does not move; what moves is which member `GET /automation/:name/runs/:runId` emits for a run nobody holds. The ruling (6399818476) names `404 RUN_NOT_FOUND` on the run-read door "the same as an unknown name"; giving the unknown-run case any other code would hand a caller the existence oracle the ruling removes. No consumer pins the old value on this door: objectui `flowResponse.ts` pins `RUN_NOT_FOUND` on the resume door, `META_ITEM_ABSENT_CODE` is the metadata door, and service-automation `paused-run-visibility.test.ts` references the message `Execution not found` only, which is unchanged. The docs row (`content/docs/automation/flows.mdx:2288`) names the message only and stays true. Declared in the changeset body.

5. **The restore door's mismatch answer equals the engine's unknown-run refusal — right.** `unknownRestoreTarget` carries `refusal: 'RUN_NOT_FOUND'`, `restoreRefusalStatus` maps it to 404, `error.code` is status-derived (as every restore refusal is), and the message `No run 'RUNID' is known` matches `engine.ts:8572` byte for byte. Cancel answers `200 { cancelled: false, notice }`, the verb's own no-run contract, with `cancelRun` never called. Screen answers the unchanged `404 No pending screen for run` ahead of the identity gate, so the answer is the same for every caller; `getSuspendedScreen` is read before the scope check but nothing from it is disclosed.

6. **Authorization is unchanged — right.** The scope check runs after `refuseUnrelatedResume`, the read gate and the operator gate, and before the verb, so a mismatched resume, cancel or restore consumes nothing. A non-starter member still meets the pre-existing 403 before any 404; the card measured that on `main` and the ruling keeps it.

7. **"Cannot prove a mismatch" falls through to the old answer — acceptable, flagged in ③.** A `getRun` throw and a `listSuspendedRuns` throw are both swallowed; when neither names an owner the door proceeds as before this card. The predicate documents this as "cannot prove", not "matches". The ruling does not ask for a fail-closed scope check; on the resume door a non-system caller is already failed closed by `refuseUnrelatedResume`, and the engine's own `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` 503 governs an unreadable store.

8. **The two adjusted pins still prove their original claims — right.** The #19987 system-context pin moves from "getRun never read" to "getRun read exactly once", with the one read named as the scope check; the #7968 throw pin moves from `mockRejectedValueOnce` to `mockRejectedValue`, since the store is read twice and an unreachable store is unreachable for both. Both carry comments saying so.

9. **The new suite is the right pin for the rule.** 25 cases over five doors: mismatch equals unknown flow, mismatch equals nobody's run, no state-changing verb called, owning flow still served, owner still found through the suspended-run list when `getRun` is blind, plus the ruling's code and status and the no-probe pass-through. The report's red-first (13 failed / 12 passed on unmodified `automation.ts`) and ablation (11 failed / 14 passed with the predicate forced `false`) are the dev's readings and are consistent with the suite's shape; not re-run here.

10. **CI on the head at 2026-10-26T05:06Z.** Concluded success: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset` (both runs), `Lint · ESLint`, every scoped lint lane, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Test Core` shards 2/8 and 8/8, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Spec property liveness`, the claim and single-writer checks. Still in progress: `Test Core` shards 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`. No run on the head has failed. This record judges on what has concluded; the queue still requires the remaining required contexts green before landing, and that is the platform's check, not this record's.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25820-automation-run-doors-flow-scope.md` declares `@objectstack/runtime: patch` and `@objectstack/spec: patch`, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` as line-initial declarations in both the changeset body and the PR body. Right on every axis: the kind is `none` (nothing a metadata author writes changes), so `patch` is the level; `@objectstack/spec` moves (a value in the exported ledger, no export added, removed or renamed, no `api-surface` shard affected, `Check Changeset` green twice); `@objectstack/runtime` is a bug fix in a released package, which takes `patch` and never `skip-changeset`. No `(widening)` or `(narrowing)` arm is owed: the accept set is unchanged (①.1, ①.4). The changeset body carries the before/after per door and the ledger note, which is the text an upgrading reader greps.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev `open_questions`: none.** Nothing to answer.
- **Dev finding 1 (message duplication, carrier none) — answered: accepted as a bounded residual, with one correction.** Both copied sentences are byte-identical to the engine at `main`: `No suspended run '${runId}'` at `engine.ts:6764` and `No run '${runId}' is known` at `engine.ts:8572`. The code comments and the PR body cite `run-resume.ts` and `consumed-suspension-restore.ts`, where neither string lives (`run-resume.ts:517` stamps `RUN_NOT_FOUND` with a different sentence for the consumed-suspension class). The risk is bounded to the message: code and status on resume come from the shared `RESUME_REFUSAL_ROWS`, and on restore from `RESTORE_REFUSAL_STATUS`. A citation fix is comment-only and is not a reason to hold this head.
- **Dev finding 2 (`flows.mdx` route table) — answered: accepted.** The row at line 2288 names the message `Execution not found`, which is unchanged; it does not state the `:name` scope or the code. Docs follow the implementation; `Flag docs affected by code changes` concluded success and the PR carries the `documentation` label.
- **Dev finding 3 (screen door keeps the status-derived code) — answered: accepted.** The ruling names the resume and run-read doors; keeping the screen door's answer exactly what it was is the ruling-neutral choice, and the row comment does not claim the screen door.
- **Reviewer flag: fail-open on an unprovable owner (①.7).** Noted, not escalated: no ruling asks the scope check to fail closed, the authority gates already do, and the degraded path answers what `main` answers today.
- **Sibling #25821 (same file) is not in this PR**, as the claim required. No `packages/spec/**` path beyond the one row the amendment approved.
- **Governed surfaces: none touched** (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success); the contract review is owed by the `packages/spec/src/**` face alone.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-g463f7`
Reviewed-by: `session_01R1q2xdtYgU6FKrZ7LgjPCC`

**VERDICT: PASS**
